reason: I'll add mucus to the colon lining to start building its protected inner wall. The picture shows the mucus as a layer above the cells.
expectation: I expect a mucus-covered lining; it may still need the supporting tissue and vessels.

alternatives.reason: The microbes and food remainder also match a goal, but I want to build the wall first.

effect: The mucus now covers the lining, so I can add the supporting tissue beneath it.
reaction: The result matched what I expected.
reason: The picture places the supporting tissue and vessels beneath the lining, so this should continue the protected wall.
expectation: I expect the mucus-covered lining to join the supporting tissue and vessels, though the muscle wall may still need adding.

alternatives.reason: The microbes can work on the food remainder, but I'd rather finish the wall first.

effect: The inner wall is complete, and the result shows it recovers water and can take in small molecules made by bacteria. I can now attach the muscle wall.
reaction: The water recovery makes sense; I’m curious about the small molecules from bacteria.
reason: The muscle wall surrounds the lining and moves contents, so joining them should complete more of the colon structure.
expectation: I expect the inner wall to fit inside the muscle wall, though the microbes will still need to work on the food remainder.

alternatives.reason: I also considered exploring what the microbes make, but I want to finish joining the wall first.

effect: The colon wall is joined, with microbes and food remnants inside and separate from the blood vessels.
reaction: The completed tube makes the layers and their jobs clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it matches the remaining goal of seeing what microbes make from fibre.
expectation: I expect the microbes to turn some fibre into smaller molecules, possibly including the fatty acids shown earlier.

effect: The result connects the bacteria to the small fatty acids shown earlier and completes the remaining goal.
reaction: I expected fatty acids, but the gas was a surprise.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the inner wall to the muscle wall made the colon's layers and how contents move through it clearer.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mucus was straightforward and felt more like setup than a decision.

surprise.text: The bacteria produced gas as well as small fatty acids, and some fibre remained.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals gave each pairing a purpose.

continue.text: I might continue to see how another body system connects to these, though the mostly straightforward pairings make me only mildly curious.
